newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials end 1996 at a record high.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials end 1996 at a record high.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares maintained their month-long bull-run on Tuesday to end 1996 on a firm note on the back of lower money market rates, good rains and forecasts of higher economic growth next year for the southern African country.

The key industrial index added 4.78 points to close at a record high of 8,786.26 after merchant banker FMB leapt 150 cents to 4,400, sugar producer Hippo rose 25 cents to 1,025, tea and coffee producers EHPL and packaging firm Hunyani added five cents each to 130 and 350 respectively.
"Shares closed this year on a very firm note and indications are that they are going to open 1997 firm," one broker said.
"Sentiment is still strong with lower rates on the money market and the falling rains," another one said.
Minings traded quietly with gold producer Ashanti unchanged at 10,000 but Wankie Colliery 40 cents higher at 600. The mining index gained 18.82 points to end at 1,083.66.
